The cause is in `src/leaks.py`, line 8:

```python
text = json.dumps(actions).lower()
```

The check serializes the transcript to JSON before searching it, and JSON escapes every backslash as `\\`. So `C:\Users\dana` in the transcript is stored as `C:\\Users\\dana` in the searched text. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so it never matches. `/home/dana` has no backslashes, so JSON leaves it unchanged and it matches.

I reproduced it from the repo root without editing anything:

- Transcript containing `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: `[]` (leak missed)
- Transcript containing `cat /home/dana/x`, secret `/home/dana`: `['/home/dana']` (leak caught)

The same thing happens with any secret containing a backslash, not only home folders. The existing tests only cover `/home/dana`, so they don't catch it. I left `src/` untouched, as you asked.
